plan_prompt:
## Settled design (nobody re-derives it)

1. **Tom's rulings, binding:** every signature belongs to a deliberately
   created identity — "it's definitely not human versus agent"; "we don't
   need guests stuff ever"; the who-are-you-here-as form dies and identity
   lives on a settings/config surface; one human (Tom) for now, externals
   arrive later by an exchange-style connection carrying their own
   identity, never by local account creation.
2. **My rulings under his delegation** (disclosed in the notice, standing
   unless he says otherwise):
   - **The key is estate-held.** Tom's identity keypair is minted by the
     estate and its private half lives beside `compose.key` in the
     estate's `.manifold/`, same custody discipline (0600, never logged,
     never serialized). It never reaches a browser. The two-browser test
     becomes two sessions of one identity.
   - **Handle: `ablative/people/tom`**, enrolled by the standing enroll op
     — the same shape every agent seat already uses. The record treats the
     human and the agents as the same kind of thing; K9 makes the door
     match the record.
   - **Unlock is a phrase.** At creation the operator sets an unlock
     phrase; the estate stores only a derivation of it (never plaintext).
     Any browser presenting the phrase is granted a session credential for
     the identity. Refused alternative, by name: reachability-as-authority
     (no factor at all) would let any tailnet visitor sign as Tom —
     dishonest signing, the exact thing this arc kills. The passkey /
     lys-capability-certificate design stays PARKED for multi-user
     (session.rs's own "increment 2" note); nothing in K9 forecloses it.
   - **The settings surface grows from the composer's proven config-panel
     pattern** (composition/compose/config-tab.ts + configuration.ts +
     controls.ts, ~1,650 LOC, COMPOSER-SPEC §3/§4) — a generalised
     surface identity joins, not a parallel invention. K9 builds the
     surface with identity as its FIRST tenant only; relocating composer
     config and the disclosure panels are later legs (survey's re-homing
     plan), and nothing here forecloses them.

## What dies (both legs carry their half)

- **Guest auto-seating at the write door.** The compose carrier's
  seat-the-unknown-signer path (admit/seating, the `Seater` publishing
  `guests/guest-<hex>` enrolls attested through @compose) is retired. An
  unenrolled signer's send refuses BY NAME; it is never seated. The
  `guests` topic never appears on a fresh record.
- **The browser-held visitor key and everything downstream of it:** the
  whole surface/page/src/identity/ directory (six modules, ~1,074 LOC:
  visitor-key, state, signed-entry, cose, naming, claim-control) and its
  consumer sites — composition/main.ts (askVisitor at boot),
  composition/compose/door.ts + seating.ts, conversation/mount.ts
  (claim control, guest naming), feed-view.ts (shortGuestName).
- **"Signed by this page" residues** — any surface language attributing an
  act to the page rather than a held identity.
- NOT dying: **historical guest entries render as ordinary members.** The
  live record holds `guests/guest-*` enrollments; they are record truth
  and keep rendering by handle like any member. Only the mint/claim/name
  machinery dies, not the rendering of what the record already holds.
- NOT dying: **the door's signed-entry verification** (lys COSE_Sign1 over
  SignedContent, the cross-language fixture). Enrolled signers may still
  present signed entries — that is the path a future foreign identity
  arrives on. What dies is seating unknowns.
- NOT dying: **the page-provenance session token** (SESSION_HEADER,
  nonce.tag MAC). Its job — "this request came from a page this estate's
  own surface served" — is orthogonal to identity and stays.

## What arrives — the ruled wire (floors; planner grounds paths/shapes)

Four verbs at the compose door, each answering with an acceptance or a
named refusal:

1. **Disclose** — does a human identity exist on this estate, and as whom
   (handle + display name). The page uses this to offer exactly one door:
   create (none exists) or unlock (one does). No identity ⇒ the page is
   read-only in the estate's honest register: controls disabled with the
   refusal in words (the declared-actions no-write-path arm, landed
   46fdbe1, is the exact precedent).
2. **Create** — handle + display name + unlock phrase. Refuses if a human
   identity already exists (Tom's externals-by-connection ruling makes one
   local human a design fact, not a cap). On acceptance: estate mints the
   keypair, holds the private half per custody above, enrolls the public
   half at the handle by the standing enroll op, answers with a session.
3. **Unlock** — phrase ⇒ session credential. Wrong phrase refuses by name.
   The credential is distinct from the page-provenance token and revocable
   estate-side (a CLI reset of phrase/sessions is in scope as the recovery
   verb; anything fancier is not).
4. **Send-as-identity** — session credential + the composed body/channel ⇒
   the DOOR builds and signs the entry with the estate-held key and places
   it on the record verbatim, exactly as the current door places a
   verified signed entry. Signing moves door-side for the human identity;
   the browser never holds key material.

Both legs build against THIS contract, not against each other's code —
the K8 pattern (ruled vocabulary, legs blind to each other).

## Leg topology (fan-out r1: isolated worktrees, disjoint file zones,
## branches merged mechanically; each brief self-contained)

- **L1 `door-identity`** — OWNS crates/ (compose carrier + any node-side
  seam the planner grounds). Content: the four verbs; guest auto-seat
  retirement; estate-held key custody + door-side signing; phrase
  derivation storage; named refusals for every arm (exists-already, wrong
  phrase, no session, unenrolled signer). RED FIRST in-leg: a test
  pinning that an unknown signer's send refuses instead of seating —
  committed failing against current admit behavior — plus the verb suite.
  Rust battery green in-leg. Report to .fleet/reports/L1.md.
- **L2 `page-identity`** — OWNS surface/page/. Content: retire
  src/identity/ + all consumer sites; the settings surface (new modules,
  house style of the config-tab pattern, every file ≤500 LOC per
  scripts/loc-gate.sh); the disclose-driven create/unlock flow; the
  session send client at the one send path (messages, poll votes, and
  declared-action presses all already route through it); read-only-with-
  words when no identity or no session; historical guest handles still
  render. Composition-suite claims covering guest flows are RE-POINTED to
  the new flow, never skipped or deleted-without-replacement. Page
  battery (tsc, composition suite, gate:dist, loc-gate) green in-leg
  against the ruled wire (door mocked at the contract, as the suite
  already fakes the door). Report to .fleet/reports/L2.md.

Merged-tree gates mine: full Rust battery + full page battery on the
merged tree, then the MANDATORY dev-estate walk at my desk — a scratch
estate through the REAL door: create at the settings surface, browser
press lands a signed entry as ablative/people/tom, second browser unlocks
the same identity, unenrolled signer refused by name, historical guest
entry renders. K8's lesson is law here: no gate pushes bytes through the
real registry — only the walk catches what the live substrate knows.
Landing after the walk, not before. Live estate untouched throughout;
deploy of the page half is a rebuild in the serving checkout, the Rust
half rides the next kernel restart (LANDED IS NOT RUNNING — said so in
the report).

## Hard walls

⛔ Live estate (ports 4176/41100-41102/9490s, every .manifold* path)
untouchable; scratch estates only.
⛔ No weakening of signature judgment anywhere: unenrolled still refuses,
malformed still refuses, the door signs ONLY under a valid session.
⛔ No foreclosure: foreign-identity-by-connection (signed-entry path
stays), passkey increment 2 (parked, named), settings-surface later
tenants (composer config, disclosure) all keep their doors open.
⛔ Key material and the unlock phrase never in logs, errors, URLs, or
serialized state — the compose.key discipline, including Debug that
never renders.

You are the PLANNER of a fleet run. Your working directory is the target repository worktree. Write .fleet/plan.md (the whole plan, every requirement anchored file:line into THIS tree) and one complete builder brief per leg at .fleet/legs/L1.md and .fleet/legs/L2.md. BEFORE minting ANY new name — wire verb paths, refusal names, facet or record kinds, key filenames, topic names — CENSUS the substrate's existing names by searching the crates/ and surface/ trees for collisions, and record in .fleet/plan.md what you searched and what you found: the previous fleet run's brief minted a facet name the registry's own admission door already owned, and only a live estate caught it. The legs will run IN PARALLEL, each builder in its own isolated worktree on its own branch — no leg sees another leg's work, and the branches are merged mechanically afterwards. Each brief must therefore be fully self-contained and independent of the other legs' outputs, and must name exactly which files its leg owns so no two legs write the same file; if the settled design forces two legs toward the same file, say so explicitly in .fleet/plan.md and assign that file to exactly one leg. Each brief is floors-not-ceilings, anchored, restates the hard walls above, and names the report file the builder must write (.fleet/reports/<id>.md). You are planning CONTENT for this fixed topology, not changing it. Commit nothing; the .fleet/ files are your only writes. When done, reply with a short summary of the plan you wrote.
